item.title: Tarique invites Japanese investment in five key sectors, including rail, technology
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday invited Japanese companies to invest in five priority sectors in Bangladesh, including automotive manufacturing, energy, technology and space, high-speed rail and logistics, and agro-processing, promising government support and reforms to improve the business environment.
Addressing the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue at JETRO headquarters in Tokyo, he said the two countries should take their long-standing relationship to a new level through trade and investment after signing the first-ever Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between Bangladesh and another country.
The forum was jointly organised by the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) and the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation (JBCCEC).
Tarique said around 350 Japanese companies are operating in Bangladesh, but Japanese direct investment remained below US$500 million, while Bangladesh’s exports to Japan stood at US$1.36 billion and imports from Japan at US$2.16 billion in the last fiscal year.
Under the recently signed EPA, 7,379 Bangladeshi products will enjoy duty-free access to Japan, while Japanese goods, including steel, automotive parts and electronic components, will receive preferential access to Bangladesh, he said.
The Prime Minister said Bangladesh has a market of more than 180 million people, a young workforce with a median age of 27 and a growing middle class. The country is expected to become one of the world’s top 10 consumer economies by 2030, he added.
He said his government has heard Japanese companies’ concerns over reliable energy, efficient infrastructure, predictable customs clearance and taxation, and was working to address them.
“I fully understand that businesses need certainty. Investors need confidence. Our job is creating the right environment to deliver both,” Tarique said.
On automotive manufacturing, he said Toyota has informed the government earlier this month of its plan to begin work on a vehicle manufacturing facility in Bangladesh, with full production targeted for 2029.
The Prime Minister said the government will provide every possible support for the initiative.
In the energy sector, he invited Japanese companies to invest in LNG infrastructure, efficient gas-fired power generation and renewable energy, saying Bangladesh has short-, medium- and long-term plans for gas and electricity development.
Tarique also highlighted cooperation with Japanese energy company JERA.
He said Bangladesh is planning to establish a Bangladesh-Japan Technology Park focused on innovation in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, robotics and electronics manufacturing, involving Japanese companies, universities and investors.
The Prime Minister also called for cooperation with Japanese institutions in space science, satellite engineering and related technologies to strengthen Bangladesh’s space capabilities.
On rail and logistics, he said Bangladesh plans to develop a nationwide elevated high-speed rail network connecting Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Rajshahi, Khulna and Barishal.
Tarique said the government plans to prepare a national master plan, assess passenger and freight demand, prioritise routes and conduct feasibility studies, inviting Japanese institutions to invest in the initiative.
He also urged Japanese companies to explore food processing and agro-based manufacturing opportunities in Bangladesh, particularly at the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone in Araihazar, which is being developed by Sumitomo Corporation to Japanese standards.
Emphasising people-to-people ties, the Prime Minister said Bangladesh wants to make Japanese-language education a priority so that millions of young people can learn the language alongside technical skills.
He said skilled Bangladeshi professionals proficient in Japanese can help meet employment needs in both Japan and Bangladesh.
Recalling Japan’s recognition of Bangladesh in February 1972 and its role as the country’s largest development partner for more than five decades, Tarique said the two countries should turn their long-standing friendship into a stronger partnership that creates opportunities for their people and shared prosperity.

item.title: Four killed in Rangpur bus-truck collision, including three garment workers
item.description:
The death toll from a collision between a passenger bus and a parked dump truck in Mithapukur, Rangpur, has risen to four, including three garment workers.
At least 14 others, including women, were injured in the accident and taken to Rangpur Medical College Hospital.
The accident occurred around 5:30am on Wednesday in front of Shah Amanat Petrol Pump at Bairagiganj Bazar in Mithapukur upazila, on the Dhaka-Rangpur highway.
The deceased were identified as Mozaffar Rahman, Golapi Begum and Alamgir Hossain, all from Phulbari upazila in Kurigram, who worked in the garment sector in Dhaka. The fourth victim was identified as Apel, a bus assistant.
According to police and local sources, a Khan Enterprise bus travelling from Dhaka to Bhurungamari in Kurigram rammed into the rear of a soil-laden dump truck parked on the highway.
Police, fire service personnel and local residents took part in rescue operations following the collision. One person died at the scene, while three others succumbed to their injuries after being taken to hospital.
Moazzem Uddin, officer-in-charge of Baradarga Highway Police Station, confirmed the four deaths. He said the seriously injured passengers were receiving medical treatment and traffic on the highway had since returned to normal.
Sardar Abdul Jalil of Rangpur Medical College Hospital also confirmed that three people brought to the hospital after the accident had died.

item.title: PM seeks Japan’s support to diversify Bangladesh’s exports
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday sought Japan’s cooperation in diversifying Bangladesh’s export basket and expanding trade and investment opportunities as the two countries look to strengthen their economic partnership.
He made the call during a meeting with Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) President Susumu Kataoka in Tokyo at 11:45am local time, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin.
The Prime Minister also called for increased Japanese investment in Bangladesh’s special economic zones, particularly in advanced manufacturing, ICT, automobiles, renewable energy and agro-processing, as he sought stronger trade and economic ties between the two countries.
He praised JETRO’s role in expanding Japanese investment in Bangladesh, saying new opportunities are emerging for Japanese companies in the country.
Both sides agreed that the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) will play an important role in strengthening bilateral trade and investment ties.
Tarique also called for Japanese support for skills development programmes and the establishment of Japanese language training centres in Bangladesh.
He said such initiatives will help create employment opportunities in Japan and strengthen the long-term economic partnership between the two countries.
JETRO President Susumu Kataoka said Bangladesh has strong investment potential because of its economic growth and geographical location.
He said Japanese companies are already showing interest in doing business and investing in Bangladesh in response to various initiatives taken by the government under Tarique’s leadership.
After the meeting, Tarique attended a luncheon hosted by Kataoka at the latter’s invitation, where they also discussed advancing bilateral cooperation and economic relations.
The Prime Minister invited the JETRO president to visit Bangladesh at his convenience.
The Bangladesh delegation included Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, PM’s Adviser on Finance and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, Invest Bangladesh Authority Chairman Ashik Chowdhury, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, PM’s Special Assistant Dr Md Shakirul Islam Khan, Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon and other senior officials from the Prime Minister’s Office.

item.title: Gold price rises by Tk2,216 per bhori after four straight cuts
item.description:
The price of gold has gone up again in the domestic market, with the cost of the best-quality 22-carat gold rising by Tk2,216 per bhori.
The new rates came into effect from 10am Wednesday, according to a press release issued by the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus).
With the latest adjustment, 22-carat gold will now sell at Tk223,074 per bhori including VAT.
Bajus said the prices of gold ornaments were adjusted following an increase in the price of refined (tejabi) gold in the local market.
Under the revised rates, the price of 21-carat gold has been raised by Tk2,100 to Tk213,043 per bhori, while 18-carat gold has gone up by Tk1,750 to Tk182,950 per bhori.
The price of gold of the traditional method has increased by Tk1,458 to Tk149,474 per bhori.
Earlier, Bajus had cut gold prices four times in a row on October 13, 22, 23 and 25, bringing down the price of 22-carat gold by a total of Tk10,439 per bhori. The latest hike comes after those four consecutive reductions.
Meanwhile, silver prices remain unchanged despite the rise in gold rates.
According to the new rates, 22-carat silver will sell at Tk3,849 per bhori, including VAT.
The prices of 21-carat and 18-carat silver stand at Tk3,674 and Tk3,149 per bhori respectively, while silver of the traditional method will cost Tk2,391 per bhori.

item.title: National Summit champions young women’s economic empowerment, leadership in Dhaka
item.description:
Save the Children in Bangladesh, with support from Unicef, hosted the "From Aspiration to Achievement: National Summit on Young Women’s Economic Empowerment and Leadership" on Wednesday in Dhaka.
Held under the Promotion of Women’s Empowerment and Resilience Building (Power) Project, the landmark summit brought together policymakers, government officials, development partners, private sector representatives, civil society organizations, and young women.
The event focused heavily on supporting adolescent girls and young women, particularly those not in education, employment, or training, by strengthening their economic participation, leadership, and resilience.
The day's high-level proceedings also featured remarks from special guest Deepa Sankar, chief of education for Unicef Bangladesh.
Highlighting the critical importance of education and skill development for youth empowerment in Bangladesh, she emphasized that non-formal education and skill training programs should no longer be viewed merely as alternative pathways, but integrated as vital components of the mainstream education system.
Another special guest Kazi Moklesur Rahman, additional secretary of the Ministry of Youth and Sports and project director of the Earn Project, highlighted the scope for institutional synergy.
He expressed his keen interest in integrating the learnings and achievements of Save the Children's Power project into the Ministry’s key initiatives, including the government's Earn project.
Mahdi Amin, adviser to the prime minister, honored the event as chief guest.
He stated that initiatives like Save the Children's Power project inspire the government to further drive the national growth narrative, particularly in youth and women's empowerment.
Emphasizing practical skill application over formal degrees, he noted: "Building practical skills is far more critical than merely acquiring academic certificates. The government is committed to collaborating with development partners like Save the Children to create such practical learning opportunities."
The day-long program featured an inaugural ceremony highlighting inspirational personal journeys shared directly by young women participants, followed by policy dialogues and panel discussions.
Sessions throughout the day centered on strengthening the ecosystem for young women's economic empowerment and bridging the gap between youth and employers for the future of work.
Through collaborative networking, exhibitions, and strategic discussions, the summit sought to chart clear pathways for advancing young women's economic independence and long-term leadership across Bangladesh.

item.title: Dhaka launches clean school pilot in 21 educational institutions
item.description:
The Dhaka district administration has launched a pilot project called “Clean School Teams” at 21 educational institutions to promote cleanliness among students and raise awareness about dengue prevention.
The initiative, which involves five institutions in Dhaka city and others across the district’s 16 upazilas, was inaugurated on Wednesday by Dhaka Divisional Commissioner Md Moniruzzaman Miah in the deputy commissioner’s conference room.
Inspired by Japan’s O-soji model, which encourages people to clean their own surroundings, the initiative aims to instil habits of cleanliness, promote respect for labour and foster a sense of responsibility among students.
Speaking at the inauguration, Moniruzzaman said the model went beyond routine cleaning and could help cultivate discipline and responsibility among students.
“When students develop the habit of keeping their own schools clean, it creates a positive ripple effect in their families and the wider community,” he said.
He added that ensuring a clean and healthy learning environment required the collective participation of teachers, students, parents and other stakeholders.
Addressing concerns about drug abuse and juvenile gangs, the divisional commissioner urged parents and teachers to remain attentive to children’s social circles and encourage them to participate in constructive activities. He said social initiatives should begin in schools and extend to families and the wider community.
Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanum said cleanliness was not merely about keeping school premises tidy but also about teaching responsibility, respect for labour and care for the environment.
“A clean school today lays the foundation for conscious and responsible citizens of tomorrow,” she said, adding that small, practical steps could help instil these values in students.
She said the initiative also aligned with the vision of building a “Green and Clean Bangladesh”.
Under the pilot project, participating schools will set aside 15–20 minutes each day for cleaning activities. Students will work in small groups to clean designated areas, including classrooms, corridors and libraries, under teachers’ supervision. School staff will remain responsible for cleaning toilets, drains and other potentially hazardous areas.
The programme will also include weekly inspections to identify dengue risks, such as stagnant water and uncovered containers that could serve as breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes. Schools will document their findings and follow-up measures using checklists.
Under the “My Home, My Responsibility” initiative, students will receive weekly checklists encouraging them to keep their living spaces tidy, dispose of waste properly and prevent water from accumulating around their homes. Teachers will review the checklists every Sunday.
Participating schools will introduce waste segregation systems for biodegradable, recyclable and other waste. Students will also learn how to produce organic fertiliser from biodegradable materials.
The administration has proposed a “Clean School Challenge” to assess institutions based on cleanliness, dengue prevention, waste management and student participation. The best-performing schools, classes and students may receive certificates, books, educational materials or saplings.
The project was initiated by Farida Khanum to extend cleanliness practices beyond school premises and encourage students to spread the message among their families and communities.
On July 8, the Dhaka district administration began forming Clean School Teams in educational institutions across the district. A subsequent three-month research period involved reviewing school activities and studying successful cleanliness models in other countries.
The administration then developed an implementation strategy adapted from Japan’s O-soji model to suit Bangladesh’s context.

item.title: Mild heat wave sweeps Dhaka, parts of Bangladesh

item.title: Education must remain inclusive
item.description:
We agree with Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon that religious education can play a significant role in shaping more responsible citizens.
Integrating moral values, integrity, and spiritual literacy into national curricula can certainly help stem social degradation and foster conscientious youth. Merely striving for efficiency and growth are meaningless if fellow citizens lack empathy and care.
With that said, in a nation built upon pluralism and constitutional guarantees of equal rights, regardless of one’s religion or faith, state policy regarding moral and religious education must strictly reflect our diverse national fabric.
If we are to educate our children about religion and faith, and expect them to be able to take the lessons they provide, then we must simultaneously ensure that no single faith receives majoritarian preference while neglecting the rest.
Bangladesh is home to millions of Hindu, Buddhist, Christian, and ethnic minority citizens, among other faiths, whose traditions and values are integral to our national identity.
As such, when state officials frame moral development through the prism of a single religion, they risk alienating minority students and eroding the inclusive foundation of public education.
Every child attending a state school or general institution deserves access to moral instruction that honours, reflects, and respects their own heritage and faith, rather than being subjected to a standardized framework that treats non-majority traditions as an afterthought.
Modernizing our national education system therefore requires a delicate balance between core ethical values and secular inclusivity.
While streamlining madrasa education with mainstream science, arts, and technology is a welcome effort to bridge structural disparities that have existed for too long, national policy must also ensure that general public schools remain welcoming spaces for students of all backgrounds.
A truly progressive curriculum must emphasize universal values -- integrity, tolerance, civic responsibility, and mutual respect -- alongside comprehensive, high-quality instruction regarding students’ respective faiths. That should be the goal.

item.title: Parties must prioritize national stability
item.description:
The attack on the central office of the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) in Dhaka’s Paltan area is a deeply disturbing reminder of the partisan hostility still poisoning our political landscape.
When political offices are stormed, vandalized, or targeted by mobs over alleged slogans or ideological grievances, democratic norms are fundamentally violated.
Reverting to street-level violence, intimidation, and reflexive mudslinging exposes a reckless disregard for civil order at a time when the nation can least afford political instability.
Instead of taking immediate responsibility or condemning mob behaviour, the immediate aftermath of the incident reduced to predictable finger-pointing, partisan denial, and blame-shifting.
This toxic reflex must end if we are to make any progress as a nation.
Political parties across the spectrum - whether in government or opposition - must recognize that their primary duty is to the citizens of Bangladesh, not to settle petty political scores or establish dominance through intimidation.
At a moment when the country is confronting severe economic pressures, turning political rivalries into physical clashes is an unpardonable distraction from the urgent work of national governance.
Allowing partisan mobs to operate with impunity under the guise of political grievance invites lawlessness and further fractures. Violence cannot be normalized as a tool for political expression.
Law enforcement agencies must investigate the Paltan attack with absolute impartiality, identifying and prosecuting the perpetrators regardless of their political affiliations.
The leadership of all political parties must also issue an unequivocal, zero-tolerance directive to their cadres against mob violence and political thuggery.
Bangladesh's democratic space has all but eroded, and we cannot think of reviving it if political dissent is met with bricks and iron rods. It is time for our political parties to focus their energies on what matters -- constructive policy, economic stabilization, and public service.

item.title: Spain: At least 10 dead in high-speed train crash
item.description:
At least 10 people were killed in a train crash in central Spain on Wednesday morning, local authorities have confirmed.
“The information we are receiving is not good at all,” a spokeswoman for the government of the Castilla-La Mancha region told local media. “There are at least 10 dead and it is possible that the number will increase.”
“There has been a collision between two trains [and] there are injured people,” added Manuel Galans, mayor of the town of Urda in the province of Toledo, near to where the incident took place just after 9am local time.
The mayor of another nearby village, Jesus Perez of Los Yebenes, told Spanish TV that the accident appeared “serious.”
Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia told local broadcaster TVE that it was a “high impact accident, it will be a major tragedy” but said it was too soon to confirm a final casualty figure.
“We don’t just need help from nearby hospitals, we need nearby hospitals that have ICU beds,” she added.
The cause of the collision was not immediately known, but initial reports suggested one train had slammed into the back of another train which had been stationary.
Images from the scene showed at least two severely damaged train carriages flipped over on their side after tumbling down an embankment.
One of the trains, operated by AVE, was reportedly carrying 397 passengers while the other, operated by IRYO, had 146 people on board, according to the Castilla-La Mancha local government spokeswoman.
A reporter for local broadcaster TVE described scenes of “absolute chaos” and a constant stream of ambulances and emergency vehicles.
El Pais cited witnesses describing numerous injuries and ​arrival of emergency medical teams at the scene.
“All resources are currently being deployed,” spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services told the AFP news agency, including “several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units.”
In a post on social media, rail operator Adif confirmed that “traffic ​on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line ​has been suspended following a rear-end collision ​between two trains.”
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was “shocked” by the “serious” accident.
“Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations,” he wrote on social media. “My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families.”
It’s not the first train crash in Spain this year. In January, 45 people died when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train.

item.title: Three killed by storm in southern India
item.description:
Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, killing at least three people before the storm weakened, officials said.
Cyclone Arnab hit southeastern Andhra Pradesh state as a “very severe cyclonic storm,” with winds of 125-135 kilometers (77-84 miles) per hour and gusts reaching 150 kph in the early hours of Wednesday morning, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
Torrential rain was recorded -- as much as 30 centimeters (nearly 12 inches) in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha states, IMD said, with the storm weakening into a “deep depression” throughout Wednesday afternoon.
“Three people have lost their lives, and 31 homes have been damaged,” Narendra Singh Bundela, Inspector General of India’s National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) told reporters.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu thanked officials who had “worked tirelessly throughout the night.”
Around 50,000 people were told to move to safer areas in Andhra Pradesh and another 48,000 in neighboring Odisha.
“Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water,” said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name and had been taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada.
Overnight, gales battered trees and heavy rain lashed the port city of Kakinada, close to the heart of the storm, as powerful waves crashed ashore.
Residents on Wednesday emerged onto flooded streets to what appeared to be limited damage in the city.
Emergency officials were also busy clearing uprooted trees and other debris from affected roads in the coastal region.
“Thank God, there was not as much damage this time,” said businessman Hussain, 43, who uses one name.
Sadiq, 40, a Kakinanda city resident, told AFP that the situation had become “very dangerous” on Tuesday night, but early warnings from authorities had helped people prepare.
“Many people locked their houses and moved to safer places”, he said.
Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean.
The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has contributed to unprecedented warming.
Neighbouring Sri Lanka and Nepal had also issued warnings.
Nepal’s disaster authority warned that the storm would move inland towards the Himalayas, bringing heavy rainfall and “a high risk of heavy snowfall, snowstorms and avalanches”.

item.title: Trump says Putin-Zelensky meeting to be set up ‘very soon’
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky would be set up “very soon.”
The announcement came as Trump’s administration ramps up diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year.
“There’ll be a meeting set up very soon and I think a lot of progress could be made,” Trump told reporters.
Zelensky said on Sunday that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November, aiming to restart stalled peace talks.
The Kremlin had previously said that a meeting between the three countries was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November.
Putin, who ordered the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine.
Trump came to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours -- but over a year of US-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough, with tens of thousands killed.
In recent days Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war.

item.title: Netanyahu bloc leads as Israeli votes counted, but no majority
item.description:
The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after two-thirds of the votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.
Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas's October 7, 2023 resistance campaign.
Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority.
With 66% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc was shown to have 54 of the 120 seats in the parliament.
Eisenkot's opposition bloc had 48 seats and the country's non-aligned Arab parties 18. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted.
Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu's hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority.
The strongest gains went to Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel.
The partial results suggest that Eisenkot's bloc would have enough seats for a majority if it entered into a coalition agreement with the Arab parties, something most of its members expressed reluctance to do on the campaign trail.
But Yair Golan, the head of Israel's main left-wing party, which is part of Eisenkot's camp, called for precisely that on Wednesday.
"We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he said on X. "We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens."
Eisenkot had said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy.
Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes on an ad hoc basis, enabling him to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition.
A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail.
A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.
Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning.
Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3am (0100 GMT) on Wednesday morning, called for a "strong government of the right" and said the "Jewish and Zionist majority must unite."
The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory.
US President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped "a lot."
Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use renewed war to push for a unity government.
"Netanyahu, don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.
He called Netanyahu "a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people's trust."
The vote came as Israel faces increasing isolation on the world stage, driven by the wars in Iran and Gaza, as well as soaring settlement construction and violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu's views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive that has reduced the territory to rubble.
But he has vowed to create a more inclusive atmosphere inside Israel, repair its international standing and rein in violent West Bank settlers.
After a turnout of nearly 78 percent, the highest since 1999, Eisenkot said it would be a mistake to hold a second election and vowed to work "swiftly" to form a government.
"The public has voted for change," he said. "A worthy leader would accept the people's vote of no confidence and announce his retirement from political life today."
Exit polls had shown Israeli Arab lists projected to win 18 or 19 seats, a sharp gain.
Arab Israelis, also known as Palestinian citizens of Israel, account for about 21% of the country's population.

item.title: Bangladesh, Japan sign 6 instruments, pledge loans worth $295m
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan have signed six bilateral cooperation instruments and pledged two yen-loan projects worth about US$295.5 million during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s four-day official visit to Japan, expanding cooperation in maritime security, investment, agriculture, fisheries, skills development and climate change.

The agreements and pledges form part of the outcomes of the prime minister’s visit from 26 to 29 October at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi, said Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin.  

The six signed instruments include a grant agreement worth up to 2.2 billion Japanese yen (US$13.44 million) for providing a patrol vessel to Bangladesh to strengthen its maritime security capabilities.

The other instruments cover economic relations and improvement of the business environment, agricultural cooperation, employment and skills development, fisheries and livestock, and climate change cooperation.

The two governments also pledged yen loans of 15.88 billion yen (US$100.8 million) for improving the investment environment and 30.68 billion yen (US$194.7 million) for the second phase of the Upazila Governance and Development Project.

The two loan pledges together amount to 46.56 billion yen, equivalent to approximately US$295.5 million.

Under the maritime security grant, Japan will provide a patrol vessel to the Bangladesh Coast Guard to strengthen its capacity to combat maritime crimes and respond to maritime incidents and natural disasters.

The memorandum of cooperation on economic relations and improvement of the business environment was signed between Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Bangladesh’s Economic Relations Division under the Ministry of Finance.

The instrument aims to strengthen bilateral economic relations and improve conditions for business and investment.

The agricultural cooperation instrument, signed between Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Agriculture, seeks to expand cooperation and attract investment in the agricultural sector.

A separate memorandum between the Japanese ministry and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock aims to promote trade, investment, technological exchange and capacity building in fisheries and livestock.
The climate change cooperation letter of intent was signed between Japan’s Ministry of the Environment and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

The employment and skills development instrument seeks to strengthen cooperation in skills development and employment opportunities for Bangladeshi workers in Japan.

The pledged yen loan for improving the investment environment is expected to support efforts to create more favourable conditions for domestic and foreign investors.

The second loan pledge will support the second phase of the Upazila Governance and Development Project, which aims to strengthen local governance and development at the upazila level.

The instruments complement broader agreements reached during the bilateral summit between Tarique Rahman and Takaichi at the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office on 27 October.

At the summit, the two leaders agreed to upgrade the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative into a broader strategic cooperation framework titled “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity”.

During the visit, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also held meetings with Japanese political leaders, business representatives and development partners to explore further investment, technology transfer, skills development and economic cooperation.

The visit is scheduled to conclude on 29 October.

Bangladesh-Japan Ties: From development cooperation to investment partnership
item.description:
Bangladesh is seeking to transform its longstanding development cooperation with Japan into a stronger economic partnership focused on trade, investment and industrialisation. During Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to Japan, the two countries have focused on expanding existing cooperation, attracting new investment, diversifying exports, facilitating technology transfer, developing a skilled workforce and improving infrastructure.
To this end, the prime minister has held a series of meetings with leading Japanese businesses and investment organisations. The government has also pledged to introduce reforms and simplify administrative procedures to create a more business-friendly environment for Japanese investors.
According to state-run news agency BSS, Tarique Rahman held separate meetings with the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), Fast Retailing, the parent company of global clothing retailer Uniqlo, and Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Ryosei Akazawa.
The discussions covered investment opportunities in energy, information and communication technology (ICT), infrastructure, readymade garments, automobile manufacturing, renewable energy and agro-processing.
Earlier, during a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman agreed to advance economic and strategic cooperation between the two countries. Japan expressed expectations that its private sector would invest around one trillion yen in Bangladesh over the next five years, potentially creating approximately 200,000 jobs.
The two sides also agreed to expand industrial and economic cooperation centred on the Bay of Bengal to elevate bilateral relations.
Addressing the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum dialogue in Tokyo on Wednesday, the prime minister called on Japanese companies to invest in five priority sectors: automobile manufacturing; energy; technology and space cooperation; railways and logistics; and agro-processing and manufacturing.
Tarique Rahman said the two countries had a longstanding foundation of friendship and development cooperation, and that the time had come to strengthen ties through expanded trade and investment.
Around 350 Japanese companies are currently operating in Bangladesh, he said, while Japan’s foreign direct investment in the country remains below $500 million. In the latest fiscal year, Bangladesh earned $1.36 billion from exports to Japan, while imports from the country totalled $2.16 billion.
He said Bangladesh’s market of more than 180 million people, young workforce and expanding middle class offered significant opportunities to expand manufacturing and exports.
Highlighting the potential for Japanese investment in automobile manufacturing, the prime minister said Toyota had announced earlier this month that it planned to begin work on establishing a vehicle manufacturing plant in Bangladesh, with full-scale production targeted for 2029. He assured the company of the government’s support for the initiative.
In the energy sector, he invited Japanese investors to explore opportunities in liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, efficient gas-fired power generation and renewable energy.
He also outlined plans to establish a Bangladesh-Japan Technology Park, inviting Japanese companies, universities and investors to participate in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, robotics and electronics manufacturing.
To improve rail connectivity and logistics, Tarique Rahman spoke of plans to develop a nationwide elevated high-speed rail network connecting major cities, including Dhaka, Chittagong, Sylhet, Rajshahi, Khulna and Barisal.
He sought technical and investment support from Japanese companies to prepare a master plan, conduct feasibility studies, assess passenger and freight demand, and determine suitable routes.
Highlighting opportunities in agro-processing and manufacturing, the prime minister said Bangladesh produced a wide variety of crops, fruits and vegetables that Japanese companies could process for domestic consumption and export-oriented industries.
He also invited Japanese investors to explore opportunities at the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone in Araihazar.
Expanding investment in Bangladesh’s readymade garment industry featured prominently during the visit.
At a meeting with a delegation led by Tadashi Yanai, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Fast Retailing Co Ltd, yesterday morning, Tarique Rahman called for increased investment in Bangladesh.
He particularly emphasised investment in man-made fibres, technical textiles and sustainable clothing production. The discussions also covered technology transfer, skills development, product innovation, advanced manufacturing systems and environmentally friendly production processes.
The prime minister said the government was ready to support the expansion of Uniqlo’s operations in Bangladesh, including through land allocation, investment approvals and simplified administrative procedures.
Later, at a meeting with JETRO President Susumu Kataoka, Tarique Rahman sought Japan’s cooperation in diversifying Bangladesh’s export basket.
He highlighted investment opportunities in advanced manufacturing, ICT, automobile production, renewable energy and agro-processing in the country’s special economic zones.
The prime minister also called for cooperation in skills development programmes and the establishment of Japanese-language training centres. He said a workforce proficient in Japanese and equipped with technical skills would help increase Bangladeshi workers’ participation in Japan’s labour market and strengthen long-term economic ties.
Kataoka said Bangladesh offered considerable investment potential because of its economic growth and geographical location. He added that various government initiatives had generated interest among Japanese companies in doing business and investing in the country.
The prime minister also held talks with JBIC to strengthen investment and economic cooperation in energy, ICT and infrastructure.
At a meeting with JBIC Governor Kazuhiko Amakawa on Wednesday morning, Tarique Rahman proposed opening an office of the institution in Bangladesh.
Amakawa said the proposal would be considered seriously.
During the meeting, the prime minister appreciated JBIC’s contribution to Bangladesh’s economic development, noting that the institution’s priority projects aligned with the current government’s development priorities.
Tarique Rahman said the government was committed to introducing investment-friendly policies and improving the business environment. Reforms were under way to simplify regulations and attract both domestic and foreign investment.
The prime minister also met Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Ryosei Akazawa on Wednesday.
Akazawa expressed interest in increasing Japanese investment in Bangladesh. Both sides agreed to explore further investment opportunities by capitalising on the interest of Japanese businesses and strengthening bilateral relations.
Both countries see the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) as an important instrument for expanding bilateral economic relations. Signed earlier this year, the agreement is Bangladesh’s first of its kind with another country.
The prime minister said 7,379 Bangladeshi products would receive duty-free access to the Japanese market under the agreement. In return, Japanese products, including steel, automobile parts and electronic components, would receive preferential market access in Bangladesh.
Both countries have emphasised the need to implement the EPA and expand trade and investment.
Addressing concerns raised by Japanese investors, Tarique Rahman said the government was prioritising reliable energy supplies, efficient infrastructure and greater predictability in customs and taxation.
He said businesses needed certainty and investor confidence, adding that the government’s responsibility was to create an environment that ensured both.
Expanding employment opportunities for Bangladeshi workers in Japan and promoting skills exchange between the two countries also featured prominently in discussions during the visit.
The prime minister emphasised the need to develop a skilled workforce through Japanese-language education and technical training.
Speaking at an exchange with expatriate Bangladeshis at the New Otani Hotel in Tokyo on Wednesday evening, Tarique Rahman said the government planned to give students opportunities to learn foreign languages, including Japanese, German and French, alongside English.
He expressed hope that the programme would begin in schools next year.
Responding to a question from expatriates, the prime minister said Bangladeshi workers needed proper training, proficiency in Japanese and an understanding of Japanese culture to strengthen their position in Japan’s labour market.
He said these preparations would help sustain the acceptance of Bangladeshi workers in the long term.
Outlining plans to improve healthcare services, Tarique Rahman said the government planned to increase the number of beds in upazila-level hospitals from 50 to 150 over the next five years.
The plans also include introducing dialysis facilities at the upazila level and expanding specialised healthcare services for women and children.
He further announced plans to recruit 100,000 health workers to raise health awareness in villages, with at least 80% of the proposed recruits being women.
At another exchange with expatriate Bangladeshis, the prime minister outlined his goal of making Dhaka and the rest of the country cleaner, less polluted and healthier.
Expressing his ambition to make Dhaka as clean as Tokyo, he said initiatives were being taken to reduce air pollution, improve the environment and plant trees in different areas.
Tarique Rahman said the government’s priority was to ensure that the benefits of reforms reached marginalised communities and working people. He added that initiatives in education, healthcare and environmental protection should directly benefit the wider population, seeking cooperation from expatriates and people across the country to implement the plans.
Bangladesh and Japan have maintained development cooperation ties for more than five decades. Japanese assistance has played an important role in Bangladesh’s development in several sectors, including infrastructure, connectivity, electricity, human resource development and capacity building.
During Tarique Rahman’s latest visit, the focus has been on building on that legacy by expanding private investment, technology transfer, industrialisation and employment opportunities.
However, the tangible benefits of these initiatives will depend on the implementation of investment proposals, improvements in the business environment and effective follow-through on the agreements and understandings reached between the two countries.

item.title: Heart patients wait months as two OTs lie idle at NICVD
item.description:
Two cardiac operating theatres remain out of service at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD), leaving patients waiting months for surgery at one of Bangladesh’s most important public heart hospitals.
The shortage has hit children with congenital heart disease particularly hard. With just one operating theatre dedicated to paediatric cardiac surgery, the hospital can perform only around 20 to 24 such operations a month, despite growing demand.
For many families unable to afford private treatment, the wait is unavoidable, even when doctors have advised surgery.
Rabeya Khatun and her husband travelled from Cumilla to Dhaka with their two-year-old daughter, who suffers from congenital heart disease.
They visited NICVD twice in September but could not get their daughter admitted because no bed was available.
The child was finally admitted on October 10. Yet the family was told she might have to wait more than two months for open-heart surgery.
After struggling to secure a hospital bed, they now face another prolonged period of uncertainty over when their daughter will receive treatment.
Other patients are being forced to return home without even securing a surgery date.
Arefin, 43, from Sundarganj in Gaibandha, was advised to undergo bypass surgery after doctors diagnosed blockages in his coronary arteries.
But he could not obtain a surgery slot.
Unable to pay for an operation at a private hospital, he decided to return home and try again after a week.
His experience reflects the difficulties facing patients who depend on subsidised cardiac treatment but cannot secure timely access to surgery.
Doctors warn that prolonged delays can increase the risk of complications for patients requiring urgent procedures.
Repeated hospital visits also add to families’ travel, accommodation and treatment expenses.
NICVD has 1,250 beds and handles an enormous volume of patients from across the country.
According to hospital figures, more than 200,000 patients received outpatient treatment in 2025, while emergency services handled approximately 250,000 patients.
The hospital recorded around 112,000 admissions during the year.
Yet only 1,972 major surgeries were performed, alongside 16,269 minor procedures.
The hospital has 10 operating theatres, including seven designated for cardiac surgery and three for vascular surgery.
Of the seven cardiac OTs, two are currently out of service because their operational equipment has exceeded its prescribed service life.
Among the five remaining theatres, three are assigned to adult cardiac surgery, one to paediatric cardiac surgery and another to infection-control-related activities.
The paediatric cardiac surgery department has 44 beds but only one dedicated operating theatre.
It also has a 10-bed postoperative intensive care unit, of which four beds are equipped with ventilators.
Hospital authorities say the department can perform approximately 20 to 24 operations a month.
With limited surgical and postoperative care capacity, children requiring heart operations can face extended waits.
NICVD Director Prof Dr Abdul Wadud Chowdhury acknowledged the difficulties caused by prolonged hospital stays.
He said patients face rising treatment costs and a greater risk of infection when they remain admitted for extended periods.
Their relatives also suffer financial and emotional strain from the additional time and expense involved.
“Some operating theatres have exceeded their service life. We are preparing a Development Project Proposal for setting up three new OTs,” he said.
A separate proposal is also being prepared to develop vascular surgery facilities.
However, these projects remain at the planning stage, offering no immediate solution for patients already waiting.
The director said the hospital must first operate on patients who have previously received surgery dates before accommodating new cases.
He acknowledged that even with additional facilities, the pressure of patients seeking treatment would make it difficult to eliminate long waits entirely.
For families such as Rabeya’s, the consequences are immediate: a child has finally secured a hospital bed, but the operation she needs may still be months away.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: Bangladesh, Japan sign six instruments, pledge two loan projects during PM’s visit
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan have signed six instruments and pledged two loan projects during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s four-day visit to Japan, aimed at strengthening coastal security, improving the investment climate and expanding cooperation in skills, agriculture and climate change.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced the agreements and loan commitments at a press briefing at the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo on Wednesday, the third day of the prime minister’s visit.
Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon also spoke at the press briefing.
Humaiun Kobir said the instruments include four memorandums of cooperation (MoCs) and a grant agreement.
Beyond these government-level agreements, 17 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) have been signed between private-sector entities at the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), he said.
The grant agreement provides up to 2.12 billion yen ($13.44 million) for the provision of a patrol vessel to strengthen Bangladesh’s coastal security capabilities.
The two countries also signed an MoC on economic relations and improving the business environment between Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Bangladesh’s Economic Relations Division under the Ministry of Finance.
Another MoC was signed between Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Agriculture.
A separate MoC was signed on the Employment for Skill Development Programme (ESDP).
The two sides also signed an MoC between Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock to promote cooperation in the fisheries and livestock sectors.
The sixth instrument was a Letter of Intent on climate change cooperation between Japan’s Ministry of the Environment and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change.
Apart from the six instruments, Japan pledged two loan projects to support Bangladesh’s development – a yen15.88 billion ($100.8 million) project to improve the investment environment and a yen30.68 billion ($194.7 million) loan for the Upazila Governance and Development Project (Phase 2).

item.title: Nahid accuses BNP of killing its own men amid ‘worsening’ law and order
item.description:
Chief Whip of the Opposition and National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam on Wednesday accused the ruling BNP of killing its own people, alleging that the “deteriorating” law-and-order situation has left ordinary people vulnerable to violence and injustice.
"How bad must the law-and-order situation have become for them to be killing their own people? Whether justice will be served for this is a question for me," Nahid said at a meeting with leaders of the Dhaka division (Southern Region) to discuss organizational progress and plans for the upcoming election.
Briefing journalists at the start of the meeting, he alleged that the judiciary remains under the “control of those in power as the justice system has not been reformed”.
Nahid alleged that cadres operating under BNP's patronage are killing even their own party men and torturing and oppressing ordinary people across the country.
"If we let this government off the hook, who knows, we may have to face another fascism. We do not want to have to overthrow another fascist regime at the cost of 1,400 lives again," he said.
Claiming that the country is turning into a "mafia state", the NCP leader said, "We wanted a neutral and strong position from the law enforcement agencies. But we see the IGP talking about crossfire. The home minister has completely failed to provide leadership. No action is being taken against the numerous drug spots that have been identified across the country. Bangladesh has effectively become a mafia state, which it already was – nothing has changed."
He alleged that while terrorists are armed, ministers and state ministers are also carrying “weapons”. "This is what is called a mafia state, where you have to confront arms with arms in your own hands," he said.
On drug trafficking, Nahid accused the government of failing to arrest the alleged godfathers of the trade, members of drug syndicates and political leaders linked to the business. "Unless this is done, it will not be possible to eliminate drugs," he said.
He also alleged that the largest volume of drug smuggling in Bangladesh takes place through Cox's Bazar, the home minister's constituency, yet he is unable to stop it even in his own area.
Referring to the upcoming local government elections, the NCP leader expressed his doubts about the polls being fair.

item.title: 24 Copa del Rey matches postponed after deadly train crash
item.description:
Spain’s national football federation has postponed all 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday following a train crash in central Spain that killed at least 30 people.
Authorities said around 80 people were injured in the accident, and the death toll could rise. The crash occurred when a high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped on the track.
“Shocked by the tragic train accident,” the federation said in a statement, adding that it had postponed the matches “in solidarity with the victims.”
“The entire Spanish football community stands united in grief over this tragedy and has made itself available to the authorities to assist the victims of this devastating accident,” it added.
The federation said it would announce a revised tournament schedule later.
However, the first-round matches scheduled for Thursday will go ahead as planned. Matches were also played on Tuesday.
The Spanish league has not announced any postponements for this weekend’s fixtures.

item.title: Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappe comments
item.description:
Real Madrid apologised to China on Wednesday after star striker Kylian Mbappe apparently joked about Mao Zedong in comments that sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV.
Mocking former leader Mao -- blamed by historians for millions of deaths -- is taboo in China, and Mbappe's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing.
In a clip of a video interview with French show "The Bridge" -- since taken down -- Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator", an apparent reference to Mao.
Real Madrid "wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any offence caused by the recent remarks of our player Kylian Mbappe", the club said in a statement.
"The club joins in the public apology issued by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself expressed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people," the 15-time European champions said.
The statement came a day after Mbappe issued his own apology, saying: "My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world."
Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made."
La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said Tuesday it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".
Earlier, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial that it was "not difficult to see that the club's longstanding tolerance of such behaviour has contributed to Mbappe's latest offensive remarks".
Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground.
CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of La Liga, the world's second-richest football league after England's Premier League.
Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist.
"His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated," wrote one user on social media platform Weibo.
Mbappe's original joke about Mao was not reposted -- or had been scrubbed -- from China's tightly controlled social media.
Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe's account, where he has over a million followers.
The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that "the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention".
Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo.
An AFP search on Dior and Hublot's Weibo page with Mbappe's Chinese name produced no results.
Offline too the Mbappe brand appeared to be under threat.
When AFP visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing's Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid shirts were available for sale, but none bearing the striker's name.
Chinese state media have previously praised Mbappe as a "footballing sensation" and "talent".
His face is plastered on billboards, on soft drinks and across social media.
Mbappe is sometimes affectionately referred to as "Guigui", meaning "turtle" in Chinese, for his resemblance to a character from the "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" movie.
Other major overseas sports leagues have previously angered China.
China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019.
This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting "Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong", referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious.
"Respecting the history, culture, social customs and national sentiments of others is a fundamental principle for cross-border interaction, a standard of conduct widely upheld by the international community," the official People's Daily newspaper said in an opinion piece.

item.title: Minister: Health sector to undergo major overhaul in two years
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain has said the government will bring sweeping changes to the country’s health sector within the next two years to ensure that no patient needs to travel to India for treatment.
“We want our patients to return home for treatment instead of going abroad,” he said while speaking at the inauguration of a primary healthcare programme in Kasba upazila of Brahmanbaria on Wednesday.
The programme, jointly organised by Rahman Development Foundation and Shakti Foundation, aims to ensure primary healthcare services for residents of Kasba and Akhaura upazilas.
The minister alleged that widespread corruption crippled the health sector under the previous regime, with large sums embezzled through procurement and tender manipulation. Many medical equipment purchased at high costs remain unusable due to a lack of manpower, he said.
He said the government, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards corruption and was taking steps to improve healthcare services nationwide.
The government plans to upgrade every upazila health complex to 151 beds, establish modern pathology facilities and introduce kidney dialysis services within two years. Each facility will also have 20 beds for mothers and 20 for children, he said.
The minister said tenders worth Tk16,000 crore for healthcare infrastructure, including upazila and union-level facilities and family welfare centres, would be floated within 15 days, with construction expected to be completed within two years.
He added that the government planned to recruit 41,391 healthcare workers this year, including nurses and midwives, and introduce robotic surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
The minister also warned private clinics operating near government hospitals against irregularities, saying no new clinic would be permitted within one kilometre of a government hospital. Existing facilities would face action if found violating regulations.
He announced that the shortage of doctors in Kasba and Akhaura would be addressed within a week, warning that absent physicians could lose their jobs.

item.title: Man killed over soil business dispute in Lakshmipur
item.description:
A 45-year-old man was shot dead allegedly by rivals over a dispute involving the soil business in Dilsadpur village of Parbatinagar union in Lakshmipur Sadar upazila on Wednesday, marking the second murder in the upazila in three days.
Hearing gunshots, Khorshed Alam’s wife, Akleema Akter, rushed out of their house and found him bleeding from a gunshot wound to the chest. Locals tried to take him to hospital, but he died before reaching the facility.
Khorshed leaves behind two sons and a daughter. Police said he had several cases filed against him, including murder, arms and drug-related cases, reports Bangla Tribune.
Akleema said two men, identified as Morshed and Majid, called her husband out of the house around 1:30pm. She also alleged that a man named Walid had previously threatened Khorshed over the soil business and suspected that those involved in the threats might have been behind the killing.
Akleema expressed concern for her own safety and that of other family members.
Hospital sources said Khorshed’s relatives took him to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital, where he was declared dead. His body was later kept at the hospital morgue for an autopsy.
Officer-in-Charge of Lakshmipur Sadar police station Wahid Parvez said several law enforcement teams were working to identify and arrest those involved.
Earlier, police recovered the body of Zakir Hossain from a betel nut garden in the Deputy Bari area of Purba Nandanpur village under Dakshin Hamsadi union in Lakshmipur Sadar upazila around 1am on Monday.
The body bore marks of sharp-force injuries to the neck. Police initially suspected that the killing might have stemmed from a dispute over drug dealing.
Zakir was the son of Tofayel Ahmed of Purba Nandanpur. Police said he had several cases filed against him involving arms and drugs.

item.title: Private ambulance owners suspend strike for 7 days at DMCH
item.description:
Private ambulance owners, who went on strike at the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) demanding a designated parking area there, have suspended their strike for seven days.
Badal Madbor, general secretary of the Bangladesh Private Ambulance Owners’ Welfare Cooperatives Society, confirmed the decision on Wednesday evening.
“We have given the hospital authorities seven days to meet our demand. If they fail to implement the demand within this period, we will announce further programs,” he said.
Earlier, the ambulance owners began the strike on Tuesday morning, demanding a permanent parking facility for private ambulances within the hospital premises.
The strike caused immense suffering for patients and their relatives, who struggled to find ambulances to take critically ill patients to other hospitals or transport bodies home.
Some families were forced to carry the bodies of their loved ones in CNG-run auto-rickshaws or covered vans.
Since Wednesday morning, relatives of patients were seen waiting for ambulances outside the hospital’s emergency department, near both the old and new buildings, and the outpatient department.
Relatives of some patients alleged that they did not receive the necessary assistance even after contacting the national emergency service 999.
Badal Madbor earlier said around 120 to 130 ambulances usually serve nearly 4,000 patients at the DMCH.
However, police often fine or impound ambulances that are parked on nearby streets due to the lack of a designated parking area, he said.
The organization’s general secretary said the ambulance owners previously renovated a space beside the hospital’s old building at their own expense but were later forced to leave the area.
They are willing to pay the government but want a designated place to park their vehicles, he added.
DMCH Director Brigadier General AKM Farhad Hossain, however, said there is no provision for parking private ambulances on government premises.
He said ambulance owners are not barred from operating their businesses but have to keep their vehicles outside the hospital premises.
Farhad said the officer-in-charge of Shahbagh Police Station has been assigned to oversee the situation.
He also said discussions were held with higher authorities about increasing the number of ambulances serving patients at the DMCH.

item.title: SAU students protest Secretariat plan, damage fair structures in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar
item.description:
Students of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University (SAU) vandalized structures being built for two fairs at the old trade fair ground in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka, on Wednesday, protesting a plan to relocate the Secretariat there.
The university authorities later intervened and brought the students back to campus.
Police and people involved in the fairs said preparations were underway for a month-long Asia International Trade Fair and a week-long Youth Fair at the site, with gates and stalls being constructed for both events.
People involved in the construction alleged that 70-80 SAU students entered the grounds in the morning and damaged the structures. They also alleged that equipment and materials were taken away by the students, causing financial losses.
A person involved in building stalls for the Youth Fair, told Prothom Alo they had government permission to construct them and questioned why their work had been damaged over a dispute concerning the land.
SAU Acting Proctor Professor Tajul Islam said students had been protesting the Secretariat relocation plan for several days. The university administration would take steps to address their demands and prevent further vandalism, he said.
The students maintain that the old trade fair ground belongs to their university and should be returned for research activities. They oppose the proposed construction of the Secretariat there.
On Tuesday, students protested while soil testing was underway at the site for the proposed Secretariat. They took soil-testing equipment and two vehicles to the campus and boycotted classes and examinations. They also formed a steering committee to press for the return of the ground.

item.title: BNP’s Eliza Zaman set to be elected unopposed in reserved seat by-polls
item.description:
BNP-nominated candidate Eliza Zaman is set to be elected unopposed in the by-election to the reserved women’s seat No 23 in the 13th Parliament, as she is the lone candidate whose nomination paper was declared valid.
Eliza Zaman was the only aspirant to submit a nomination paper before the deadline expired on Monday afternoon, and the Election Commission published the list of the lone validly nominated candidate on Wednesday.
Her nomination paper was scrutinised on Tuesday, according to a notification signed by Md Moin Uddin Khan, returning officer for the reserved seats and EC joint secretary on Wednesday.
Eliza Zaman is also a joint convener of Pirojpur district BNP and the organising secretary for the Barishal division of the party’s women’s wing, Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal.
According to the Election Commission’s schedule, November 1 is the last date for withdrawal of candidature. Though voting is scheduled for November 12, the balloting will not be required.
Now Eliza Zaman is set to be declared elected unopposed without a formal vote if she does not quit the race by November 1.
Earlier, on October 1, BNP reserved-seat MP Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti resigned after being instructed to step down by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The Parliament Secretariat issued a gazette notification declaring the seat vacant on the same day.
The development came amid allegations of her involvement in an attack, vandalism, looting and demolition at the Radda MCH-FP Centre, a maternal and child healthcare facility in Mirpur.
The health centre was attacked and vandalised around midnight, with allegations that ruling party leaders and activists at different levels were involved.
Mishti, however, denied any involvement in the incident.

item.title: Minister: No plan to raise edible oil prices before Ramadan
item.description:
The government has no plan to raise edible oil prices before Ramadan, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Wednesday, adding that sufficient supplies of essential commodities are in the import pipeline to meet seasonal demand.
“There is no plan to increase edible oil prices at this moment,” he told journalists before a meeting with importers and traders at the Commerce Ministry in Dhaka.
Commerce Secretary Sharif Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission Chairman Nasir Ud Doula, senior ministry officials, importers and business leaders attended the meeting.
The minister said the government had reviewed the supply of import-dependent commodities, including edible oil, chickpeas, lentils and sugar, against projected demand during Ramadan.
“The volume of goods in our import pipeline is sufficient to keep the market stable. There will be no shortage of commodities during Ramadan or before or after it,” he said.
However, fluctuations in international commodity prices and shipping costs could affect import expenses and domestic prices, he added.
Noting that chickpea prices had risen slightly in the international market, Muktadir said discussions were underway with importers to ensure uninterrupted supplies and maintain market stability.
Asked whether businesses were facing difficulties opening letters of credit (LCs) for imports, he said no major obstacles had been reported so far.
If importers faced difficulties with LC margins or other banking procedures, the government would discuss the matter with Bangladesh Bank and take necessary steps, he added.
On expanding Bangladesh’s international trade, Muktadir said formal negotiations had begun on a proposed free trade agreement (FTA) with Malaysia.
The first round of talks began on Tuesday, with the government aiming to conclude the agreement by December 2027, he said.
Bangladesh is also discussing preferential trade cooperation with key partners, including the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia, Oman, New Zealand and the European Union.
The minister said retaining duty-free and preferential market access after Bangladesh graduates from the least developed country (LDC) category would be a major challenge.
FTAs could help Bangladesh maintain export competitiveness, expand markets for ready-made garments and other products, attract investment and increase bilateral trade, he added.

item.title: Japan keen to boost investment in Bangladesh, minister tells Tarique
item.description:
Japan is keen to increase investment in Bangladesh, viewing the country as an attractive investment destination, Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Akazawa Ryosei told Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday.
During a meeting with the prime minister in Japan, Akazawa expressed his country’s interest in further developing bilateral relations and expanding Japanese investment in Bangladesh, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin.
Tarique thanked the Japanese government for its continued support and cooperation in building a developed and prosperous Bangladesh.
Both sides agreed to advance cooperation in areas discussed during the recent bilateral summit between Tarique and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and further strengthen bilateral relations.
They also stressed the need to capitalise on the interest among Japanese business leaders in Bangladesh to attract more Japanese investment to the country.
Recalling the contributions of his parents to boosting Bangladesh-Japan relations, Tarique said his father, Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, and his mother, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, each visited Japan twice.
He said the development of bilateral relations continues since their time and expressed his desire to carry forward that legacy.
The prime minister also invited Akazawa to visit Bangladesh.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, Invest Bangladesh Authority Chairman Ashik Chowdhury and Bangladesh Bank Governor Mostaqur Rahman attended the meeting.
Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Dr Shakirul Islam Khan and senior officials were also present.

item.title: BB to reduce family control on bank boards
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank remains firm on its decision to reduce family control on the board of directors of private banks.
Despite pressure from bank owners, the central bank has retained its proposal to shorten the tenure of directors and limit the number of members from the same family.
In the draft amendment to the Bank Company Act sent to the Finance Division last week, a proposal was made to reduce the number of members from the same family on a bank's board of directors from three to two.
Additionally, it has been proposed to reduce the continuous tenure of directors from 12 years to 6 years, with a mandatory three-year break required before any re-appointment.
These changes were also part of the reform proposals initiated during the interim government.
The central bank, led by governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, has maintained that exact stance.
However, changes have been made to the previous proposals regarding the size of the board of directors and the number of independent directors.
In the new draft, alongside proposing a maximum of 20 board members, it has been proposed to increase the number of independent directors from two to five.
The previous proposal was to limit the number of board members to 15, with at least half the seats reserved for independent directors.
To curb political influence in loan disbursements, the new proposal suggests barring Members of Parliament (MPs), ministers, and local public representatives from becoming bank directors.
At the same time, there is a proposal to grant the central bank the authority to relax the 10 percent shareholding limit for strategic institutional investors.
Meanwhile, the Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB), an organization of bank owners, has been opposing these reforms.
They demand that the maximum number of family members on the board be kept at three and the tenure of directors be set at nine years.
These initiatives have been taken as part of restructuring the banking sector, which has been hit hard by non-performing loans.
According to a Moody's report on September 15, 32.8% of the country's total loans are defaulted.
A senior official from the Ministry of Finance said that the draft will be reviewed in an inter-ministerial meeting before being presented to the Cabinet. The government aims to table and pass the bill in the upcoming parliamentary session.

item.title: 13 EBL employees receive the Chairman Award
item.description:
